title: Expression
summary: An expression is a finite arrangement of symbols built by explicit formation rules.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared formal language context is fixed.

content.plain: An expression is a finite arrangement of symbols built by explicit formation rules.
content.exact: Given an alphabet Σ and a grammar G, Expr(G) is the least class containing the atomic expressions and closed under the constructors declared by G.
content.example: If x and y are terms and + is binary, +(x,y) may be a well-formed term.
content.caveat: Well-formedness is syntax; it does not guarantee meaning or truth.
